hook: He doesn't hit me, but **home doesn't feel safe.** Is that domestic violence?

slides.title: It's **not just** physical.
slides.body: Domestic violence includes physical, sexual, **verbal and emotional,** and economic abuse. It covers harm to your health, safety or well-being, mental or physical, and harassment over dowry.
slides.ref: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 · Sec 3

slides.title: Abuse **can look like:**
list: Taunts for not having a child or son
Denying money or resources you're entitled to
Harassing you or family for dowry

slides.title: **Who** is protected?
slides.body: A woman who lives, or has lived, in a shared household with the abuser, related by marriage, a relationship in the nature of marriage, blood, adoption or as a joint family.

slides.title: How to **get protection.**
list: See a **Protection Officer** or the police. They must tell you about free legal services.
Apply to the **Magistrate**, yourself or through the officer or someone else.
The Magistrate tries to decide within **60 days** of the first hearing.

slides.title: What the Magistrate **can order.**
list: Protection order: no violence, no contact
Residence order: you can't be pushed out
Money for expenses, losses and maintenance

slides.title: You can **stay in the home.**
slides.body: You have a right to live in the shared household whether or not you own any part of it. You can't be evicted from it except by procedure established by law.

slides.title: Breaking the order is **a crime.**
slides.body: Breach of a protection order: up to 1 year in jail, a fine up to ₹20,000, or both. It is cognizable and non-bailable. In danger? Call **181** (Women Helpline) or 112.

sources: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 – Sections 2(a), 2(f), 3, 5, 8, 12, 17, 18–23, 31, 32
Ministry of Women and Child Development – Women Helpline 181, integrated with ERSS-112 (pib.gov.in)
Official copies of the Act: Meghalaya Police (megpolice.gov.in) and S3WaaS (gov.in)
caption:
Abuse at home isn't only about being hit. Here's what the law covers and how to get protection. 👇

1️⃣ Domestic violence includes physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse
2️⃣ It protects women in a shared household: wives, women in a relationship in the nature of marriage, and family members
3️⃣ Contact your district's Protection Officer or the police, and apply to the Magistrate
4️⃣ The first hearing is ordinarily within 3 days
5️⃣ The Magistrate can order protection, residence, money, custody and compensation
6️⃣ Breaking a protection order can mean up to 1 year in jail. In danger? Call 181 or 112

Source: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (Sec 2, 3, 12, 17–23, 31, 32)
